Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are already out in the middle now. Paul Stirling and Ross Adair are the two openers for Ireland. Just like Ireland, West Indies are also going with spin as Akeal Hosein will start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Ireland, opting to bowl first, did not have the best of starts as they gave away a few loose balls, and the Men in Maroon capitalized on it. Matthew Humphreys, with 2/16 in his four overs, was the standout bowler for the home side while Barry McCarthy, Ben White, and Mark Adair took one apiece. Ireland dropped a few chances in the outfield, and it did not help them either. Right then, the home side will have to chase their highest successful score if they are to go past the winning line. Can they do it, or will the West Indies come hard with the ball and defend this score? We shall find out soon. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

A solid batting effort from the West Indies takes them to a mammoth score of 256/5 from their 20 overs. Having been asked to bat first, the opening duo of Shai Hope and Evin Lewis added 122 inside 11 overs to set a strong base. Hope departed on 51 while Lewis slammed 91 and missed out on a well-deserved hundred. Holder, Powell, and Hetmyer did not add much. Keacy Carty batted nicely on his T20I debut and made an unbeaten 49 off just 22. Some lusty blows from Romario Shepherd took the Windies past the 250-run mark.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! The two umpires walk out to the middle, followed by the Ireland players, who spread out to take their respective field positions. Evin Lewis and Shai Hope are the two openers for West Indies. We will see spin straightaway as Matthew Humphreys has the new ball in hand. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start of the game, but before the that the players from both sides line up for their respective national anthems. It will be West Indies' first, followed by the national anthem of Ireland.

Shai Hope, the captain of West Indies says that the wicket is under covers for a few days, but batters will have to assess quickly. Adds that it was a tough tour to England, but they need to take learnings from the England series and apply them here. Ends by sharing that Keacy Carty makes his debut.

Paul Stirling, the captain of Ireland, says that the pitch has been under covers and they want to take advantage of any early assistance. Adds that this is a single-game shootout, and they want to approach it with full positivity. Informs Liam McCarthy makes his debut.

PITCH REPORT - Isabel Joyce is at the pitch side. She says that the wicket has a bit of strange look since it has been under covers. She adds that it looks a bit wet, but it is pretty hard. Shares that 57m and 63m square boundaries, while the straight hit is 74m. Ends by adding that the outfield should be good and the ball should come well onto the bat.

Ireland (Playing XI) - Paul Stirling (C), Ross Adair, Harry Tector, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Tim Tector, George Dockrell, Mark Adair, Barry McCarthy, Liam McCarthy (On Debut), Matthew Humphreys, Ben White.
West Indies (Playing XI) - Evin Lewis, Shai Hope (C/WK), Shimron Hetmyer, Keacy Carty (On Debut), Rovman Powell, Romario Shepherd, Jason Holder, Gudakesh Motie, Alzarri Joseph, Akeal Hosein.
TOSS - Ireland have won the toss and elected to BOWL first.
Just In - The news from the West Indies camp is that Keacy Carty who was the star batter against Ireland in the ODI series, will be making his T20I debut in this match.

Meanwhile, the West Indies arrive with a point to prove. Despite suffering a recent T20I whitewash at the hands of England, they showed real promise in last month’s ODI series against Ireland. With explosive batters like Rovman Powell, Shimron Hetmyer, and Evin Lewis in the lineup, there's no shortage of firepower. Add to that a well-rounded bowling attack featuring Akeal Hosein’s guile, Jason Holder’s experience, and Alzarri Joseph’s raw pace, and this West Indies side has the tools to make a serious statement. Can Ireland defy expectations in this final game, or will the Men in Maroon stamp their authority on the clash? Toss and team news coming up shortly. Stay tuned!

Ireland, under the leadership of Paul Stirling, announced a well-balanced squad for the series. The seasoned quartet of Mark Adair, Harry Tector, Lorcan Tucker, and George Dockrell will provide a strong backbone, while rising stars such as Ross Adair and Matthew Humphreys are poised to seize their chances and make a mark. With the series now shortened, the hosts will be eager to strike early and shift the momentum in their favor.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the third and final T20I in the series between Ireland and the West Indies, from the Bready Cricket Club. With the first two games being washed out due to rain, it has effectively turned into a one-game shootout. All eyes will be on the weather once again as both teams gear up for a crucial clash in the shortest format.
…MATCHDAY…

The rain has been the only winner so far in this three-match T20I series, with both the opening encounters being washed out without a result. As we gear up for the third and final game, both Ireland and West Indies will be hoping for a bit of sunshine and a full contest to finally test themselves out in the middle. For the West Indies, it’s been a frustrating couple of weeks. They arrived in Ireland on the back of a demoralizing 3-0 series loss to England, where nothing really clicked, neither the experienced campaigners like and nor the younger faces could make much of a mark. However, they will still take some positives with Shai Hope and Rovman Powell showing some resistance with the bat. But they will take heart from past performances—especially Keacy Carty, who hammered back-to-back hundreds the last time these two sides met in an ODI series. He’ll be a player to watch if he gets a game here. Hope, now leading the side in T20Is, will look to bring his calm leadership and stability at the top, while Sherfane Rutherford’s and Shimron Hetmyer's power-hitting remains a big weapon in the middle overs. In the bowling department, Akeal Hosein’s control and Romario Shepherd’s pace variations could be key. Ireland, meanwhile, will want to make the most of home conditions. Paul Stirling remains their most dangerous batter on his day, and the likes of Harry Tector and George Dockrell offer middle-order solidity and a bit of flair. On the bowling front, Graham Hume’s pace and Mark Adair’s experience give them an edge, especially in seam-friendly conditions. With the series on the line, technically still tied at 0-0 - it’s now or never for both teams to come away with a win and some much-needed momentum. Fingers crossed the rain stays away!
